title: Why Is All Life Made of Cells? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
An onion peel, a scraping from inside your cheek and a drop of pond water all show tiny units under a microscope. Diya asks: why is every living thing built from these units, and who first worked this out?

You will see what a cell is, zoom from an onion peel to one cell and its nucleus, and follow the story of the cell theory step by step: Leeuwenhoek, Robert Brown, Schleiden (1838), Schwann (1839) and Virchow (1855). Then the two rules of the cell theory with a cell dividing, cell sizes from Mycoplasma to the ostrich egg, cell shapes, a pause and think check, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern match question and a recap card.

This is Episode 60 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Onion peel, cheek cells, pond water
0:35 What is a cell?
0:57 Zoom in: onion peel to nucleus
1:38 The story of the cell theory
2:35 The two rules of the cell theory
2:58 Cell sizes
3:21 Cell shapes + pause and think
4:00 Worked example: test the cell theory
4:31 Exam trap: who explained new cells?
4:48 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:13 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells. A bacterium and your cheek cell are both cells, so why are they so different?
